recentItems.title: Jerry Beck (AEA Talks - Episode 3)
recentItems.description:
AEA Talks is a new series for the channel where Griffin "The" Hansen, president of the Animation Education Association (AEA) interviews animated filmmakers about their work and career. For this episode, we switch it up a bit with a conversation between Griffin and Jerry Beck, the legendary author and educator who created the discipline of animation history. He joined Griffin to discuss his books, relationship with Leonard Maltin, and the 1964 World's Fair.

The Animation Education Association was founded in 2020 to promote and preserve America's heritage of animated film through community projects. With this new series, we extend our mission to audio interviews archiving conversations with notable animated filmmakers. These interviews will always be available (for free!) for both education and entertainment purposes. Please enjoy the interview and find books by Jerry Beck at your local bookstore or library. His blog, Cartoon Research, is an invaluable resource for scholars, and can be found here: https://cartoonresearch.com/

AEA on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Animeducassoc
AEA on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/animationeducationassociation/
AEA on Twitter: https://x.com/Animeducassoc

recentItems.title: Tomm Moore (AEA Talks - Episode 2)
recentItems.description:
AEA Talks is a new series for the channel where Griffin "The" Hansen, president of the Animation Education Association (AEA) interviews animated filmmakers about their work and career. Tomm Moore is one of the co-founders of Cartoon Saloon, Ireland’s premiere animation studio. He’s directed or co-directed films like “The Secret of Kells”, “Song of the Sea”, and “Wolfwalkers”, and executive produced Cartoon Saloon’s short film “Éiru”, which was recently shortlisted for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short. He joined Griffin to talk about his family, childhood, and Irish beer.

The Animation Education Association was founded in 2020 to promote and preserve America's heritage of animated film through community projects. With this new series, we extend our mission to audio interviews archiving conversations with notable animated filmmakers. These interviews will always be available (for free!) for both education and entertainment purposes. Please enjoy the interview and look further into the work of Tomm Moore and Cartoon Saloon here: https://www.cartoonsaloon.ie/

AEA on Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Animeducassoc
AEA on Twitter: https://x.com/Animeducassoc

recentItems.title: The Woman Who Sculpted Boston: A Conversation with Nancy Schön
recentItems.description:
Nancy Schön is Boston's greatest sculptor; her public art can be found all around the city, delighting people of all ages. "Make Way for Ducklings", "The Tortoise and The Hare", "Myrtle the Turtle", and many more make Boston a brighter place. In anticipation of Mrs. Schön's 97th birthday this month, Griffin talks to her about all things Schön!

Nancy Schön's Website: https://www.schon.com/
"Boston to Moscow", a documentary about Schön's work bringing her art to Russia: https://schon.com/boston-to-moscow/index.htm
"Make Way For Nancy", a memoir about Schön's life in the arts: https://www.schon.com/make-way-for-nancy/index.php

Thumbnail image by Jessamyn Martin. All rights reserved.

recentItems.title: Caroline Leaf (AEA Talks - Episode 1)
recentItems.description:
AEA Talks is a new series for the channel where Griffin "The" Hansen, president of the Animation Education Association (AEA) interviews animated filmmakers about their work and career. Caroline Leaf is a legendary animator and the "mother of sand animation", internationally acclaimed for films like "The Street" and "Two Sisters". She joined Griffin to talk about her college days, artistic philosophy, and lobster rolls.

The Animation Education Association was founded in 2020 to promote and preserve America's heritage of animated film through community projects. With this new series, we extend our mission to audio interviews archiving conversations with notable animated filmmakers. These interviews will always be available (for free!) for both education and entertainment purposes. Please enjoy the interview and look further into the work of Caroline Leaf. Many of her films can be accessed free here: https://www.nfb.ca/directors/caroline-leaf/

recentItems.description:
